newsitem.title: CHINA: Drought hits 3.6 mln ha crops in China's Shandong.
newsitem.headline: Drought hits 3.6 mln ha crops in China's Shandong.

text.p: The worst drought in China's eastern Shandong province for 96 years has hit 3.6 million hectares of crops, with more than 30 percent of the total dying due to lack of irrigation, the China Daily said on Wednesday.
Summer sowing on 520,000 hectares in the province that is a major producer of corn and cotton had to be suspended because of the drought, it said.
A shortage of drinking water had affected more than 3.5 million farmers and 850,000 head of livestock, it said.
The province must irrigate seven percent of China's farmland with water resources that account for just 1.4 percent of the national average, it said.

Shandong recorded only 66 mm of rain from June 1 to July 21, about 70 percent less than usual and the lowest level since 1901, it said. Temperatures have been unusually high, about 2.4 degrees Celsius above normal.
